summary.text: Ant Pitt is standing as an independent candidate for Eastern Victoria Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 election. A Gippsland Times report from June 2026, whose full text is behind a paywall, calls her a nurse and names housing and help for farmers as her two main issues. No campaign site or fuller biography had been found as at early November 2026.

previous_candidacies.note: An Antoinette Pitt headed the Australian Progressives' Senate ticket in Victoria; no source we found says this is the same person.

priorities.text: Housing
Support for farmers

summary.text: Clay Esler is a One Nation candidate for Eastern Victoria Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 election. An October 2026 copy of One Nation Victoria's candidates page called him the party's lead candidate in the region and named his issues as accountable government, community safety, affordable energy and jobs in regional areas, but gave no other biography. A local paper reported at the start of October that the party was choosing a new candidate for first place on its Eastern Victoria ticket after its original lead candidate withdrew, while Wikipedia's 2026 list names only Neil Davison for One Nation in the region.
summary.note: Ticket position: One Nation's candidates page (archived 23 Oct 2026) calls him the lead candidate for Eastern Victoria, but the tracker's ticket and Wikipedia put Neil Davison first. His own party page refuses scripts and has no archived copy, so it could not be read.

priorities.text: Accountable government
Community safety
Affordable energy
Jobs in regional Victoria

summary.text: Danielle Burridge is the Legalise Cannabis Victoria candidate for Eastern Victoria Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 election. Her party profile says she has lived in the region for close to five years and is finishing an honours research thesis in psychology. It says she came to the cause after caring for her father, who had terminal cancer and was helped by medicinal cannabis before he died in 2019.

priorities.text: My fight for cannabis law reform is personal.
Driving laws that don't penalise patients using lawfully prescribed medicinal cannabis
Affordable, compassionate access to medicinal cannabis for dying patients and their families

summary.text: Enver Erdogan is a Labor member of the Legislative Council, appointed for Southern Metropolitan Region in 2019 and elected for Northern Metropolitan Region in 2022. A minister since December 2022, he has held Corrections, Youth Justice and Environment, and is now Minister for Finance, Government Services, and Casino, Gaming and Liquor Regulation. He is reported to be on Labor's Eastern Victoria Region ticket in 2026 rather than Northern Metropolitan; neither his Parliament page nor Wikipedia confirms the move.

prior_roles.note: Appointed to fill the vacancy left by Philip Dalidakis.

summary.text: Jeff Bourman is first in the Shooters, Fishers and Farmers Party's group (I) for Eastern Victoria Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. He has represented Eastern Victoria in the Legislative Council since the 2014 election, was returned in 2018 and 2022, and founded and chairs the party's Victorian branch. Before Parliament he was a Victoria Police officer and worked in IT, among other jobs, and he has said a 2012 change to firearms rules prompted him to stand.

summary.text: Matt Green is a Liberal candidate for Eastern Victoria Region in the Legislative Council at the 2026 election, third on the joint Liberal and National ticket behind Renee Heath and Melina Bath. He works as a senior electorate officer for Wayne Farnham, the Liberal member for Narracan, and his preselection did not change that job, according to the Warragul & Drouin Gazette. His party page says he grew up in Bunyip and now lives in Warragul.

Better value for taxpayers' money in government services
Industry, innovation and technological change in government

summary.text: Melina Bath is a Nationals member of the Legislative Council for Eastern Victoria Region, chosen in 2015 to fill the vacancy left when Danny O'Brien moved to the lower house seat of Gippsland South. A former maths and science teacher who earlier ran a health food shop in Leongatha, she has led the Nationals in the upper house since 2022 and is shadow minister for public land management, Aboriginal affairs and outdoor recreation. She is recontesting Eastern Victoria Region in 2026.

summary.note: One Nation has not confirmed his ticket position, and its Victorian site refused our requests (HTTP 403).

summary.text: Renee Heath is a Liberal member of the Legislative Council for Eastern Victoria Region, elected in 2022 after winning top spot on the Liberal ticket over the sitting MLC Cathrine Burnett-Wake. Before the election the then Liberal leader said she would not sit in the party room, which his successor reversed once she was elected. She has been opposition whip in the upper house since 2025 and a shadow minister since late 2025, and is recontesting Eastern Victoria Region in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Crime Prevention and Victim Support
Opposition Whip in the Legislative Council
Shadow Assistant Minister for Victims and Crime Prevention
Shadow Assistant Minister for Multicultural Affairs
Shadow Assistant Minister for Victims of Family Violence
Secretary of the Parliamentary Liberal Party

legal_and_integrity.text: Removed as Secretary of the Parliamentary Liberal Party after the party-room meeting on Moira Deeming's expulsion, for which she had produced three versions of the minutes, one of them leaked to the media.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: Removed from the post in May 2023.

priorities.text: Cutting state debt
Helping small business recover
More capacity in the state health system
Education reform
Restoring free speech
